FLAWS in design as written: (1) NO NULL ARM. d_NS growth across n=9..15 with k=ceil(n/2) is largely dimension counting (n*C(2k,<=d-2) vs C(2k,<=d)); the null shows the same 4->5 step (by n=15) so 'd_NS increases by one step' cannot discriminate true/false; the only n where Semaev and null differ at all is n=13 (4 vs 5). (2) Hypothesis (i) d_F<=d_NS is a tautology (static rows are the first round of the closure) -- a violation would be a bug, not a result; it must be a code assertion not a prediction. (3) d_K^NS = degree of multilinear interpolant of 1/u is a unique function; for any u with generic table it is 2k (>=k trivially, any random nonvanishing table gives it), so 'd_K^NS >= k' has zero power; also u has K-degree 2 so G=1/u is a pure table quantity. (4) 'polynomial-vs-random subspace split' references a V family not defined in this idea (and MODS in ffd_semaev_core only covers n<=10; n=11,13,15,17 need added irreducibles, e.g. x^11+x^2+1, x^13+x^4+x^3+x+1, x^15+x+1, x^17+x^3+1). (5) 'unsat, exhaustively checked' is not in the library; must be added (table over 2^(2k) points). (6) False-branch 'd_NS flat at 4 across n=9..15' is already refuted by the first run (NS=5 at n>=15) and the true-branch 'd_NS-d_F in {0,1} on >=80%' is already met by construction, so as pre-registered the experiment is nearly decided before running. (7) SCALING: toy window gives two plateau values (4,5) over n=9..17; k+2 (proved bound) and the counting bound both grow linearly, so nothing here extrapolates to n=131 / l<<n regime; k=ceil(n/2) (m=2 unsat refutation regime) is not the m>=3, l~n/m regime that governs an IC. Only a closed form for d_NS(n,k) proved/validated across (n,k) could carry weight, and any such result is theory-class (no change to B*D^2; XL-only accounting).
